headline: DR Congo stops Portugal in historic match
summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo held Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal to a 1-1 draw, marking a significant achievement for the African side.
details: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) achieved a historic result by holding Portugal to a 1-1 draw in a friendly match.
The match saw both teams score one goal each, with the first half ending in a 1-1 deadlock.
The Congo side showed great resilience and resilience against the opposition, effectively neutralizing the threat of Cristiano Ronaldo and his teammates.
This result is considered a historic milestone for DR Congo football, as they stop one of the world's top-ranked teams.

headline_marked: Govt to [[build barbed-wire fences along Myanmar border]] to curb crime
headline: Govt to build barbed-wire fences along Myanmar border to curb crime
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced plans to strengthen security and stop infiltration and border killings along the Myanmar frontier.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told parliament yesterday that the government has taken initiatives to construct barbed-wire fences along the Myanmar border to strengthen security and curb border killings, infiltration, and cross-border crimes.
The minister noted that while fences have already been erected at sensitive points along the Indian border, plans for further construction are currently under consideration.
To enhance surveillance, a 'Smart Border Surveillance System' has been installed in highly sensitive areas along the southwestern and northwestern borders.
The government is also progressing with the construction of border roads in remote hilly areas to enable quicker responses to border crimes.
Addressing border killings by India's Border Security Force (BSF), the minister described the deaths of Bangladeshi citizens as 'deeply tragic' and a violation of human rights.
He stated that Bangladesh has strongly opposed the use of lethal weapons along the border and has pressed for compensation and accountability for the victims' families.
Since August 5, 2024, the BSF has pushed 2,369 people into Bangladesh; of these, 2,175 were handed over to police, 11 returned to the BSF, and 183 pushed back.
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is now using thermal imagers, night-vision devices, CCTV cameras, and drone surveillance to prevent drug trafficking and other crimes.
caption:
Bangladesh is planning to fence the Myanmar border to stop infiltration and cross-border crime.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told parliament yesterday that the government has taken initiatives to construct barbed-wire fences along the Myanmar border to strengthen security and curb border killings, infiltration, and cross-border crimes.

The minister noted that while fences have already been erected at sensitive points along the Indian border, plans for further construction are currently under consideration.

To enhance surveillance, a 'Smart Border Surveillance System' has been installed in highly sensitive areas along the southwestern and northwestern borders.

The government is also progressing with the construction of border roads in remote hilly areas to enable quicker responses to border crimes.

Addressing border killings by India's Border Security Force (BSF), the minister described the deaths of Bangladeshi citizens as 'deeply tragic' and a violation of human rights.

He stated that Bangladesh has strongly opposed the use of lethal weapons along the border and has pressed for compensation and accountability for the victims' families.

Since August 5, 2024, the BSF has pushed 2,369 people into Bangladesh; of these, 2,175 were handed over to police, 11 returned to the BSF, and 183 pushed back.

The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is now using thermal imagers, night-vision devices, CCTV cameras, and drone surveillance to prevent drug trafficking and other crimes.

#Bangladesh #MyanmarBorder #BorderSecurity #BGB #NationalSecurity

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Somoy News, bdnews24.com
